text:
maya: Heads up — we've got /health flapping on edge-nat64 pool eu-west-1, started ~12:12 UTC. ~40% checks returning 503 or timeout. infra-bot posted alert.
infra-bot: [ALERT] probe_failed service=edge-proxy pool=edge-nat64-eu-west-1 count=193 failures=76
ryan: Any recent config changes on the dns64/nat64 side? Could be translation prefix rotation.
maya: No config deploys. DNS changes? I ran: ``dig AAAA app.internal.edge.redwood.net +short`` and sometimes it returns nothing, sometimes returns the DNS64 prefix record only.
sam: I reproduced from my laptop via ipv6-only network: `curl -6 -v https://app.internal.edge.redwood.net/health` -> connection reset. When I force IPv4 (`curl -4`) it succeeds.
leila: Sounds like the LB is advertising AAAA but backend isn't reachable over IPv6; NAT64 translator is intermittently dropping sessions. Any pattern by node?
maya: Failures correlated with two nodes: edge-lb-7 and edge-lb-9. Logs show repeated `500 upstream connect error or disconnect`. Example from edge-lb-7 logs:
```:
[12:15:01] proxy error: nat64_translate: failed to allocate ephemeral port -> ENOPROTOOPT
[12:15:02] upstream connect error
```
ryan: ENOPROTOOPT is strange — could be hitting ephemeral port exhaustion on translator NAT64 implementation when many healthchecks are concurrent.
sam: Healthchecks are 10s interval x 200 targets in the pool. That's a lot of short connections. We might be exhausting SNAT ports.
leila: If it's port exhaustion, firewall/NAT64 node counters should show high connection churn. Can someone check `conntrack -S` and ephemeral port usage on those nodes?
maya: On edge-lb-7:
```:
conntrack: entries=524288 used=489123
snat_ports_in_use=64000
```
maya: Ports are near capacity, hence random failures.
ryan: Ok. Short term: reduce parallelism of healthchecks or switch healthcheck to prefer IPv4 (curl -4). Long term: increase ephemeral port range or add more NAT64 translators / distribute healthchecks across more nodes.
leila: We should also change DNS to not advertise AAAA to clients known to be IPv4-only to avoid forcing NAT64. But internal services are dualstack — tricky.
sam: Proposed quick fix: change pool healthcheck to use v4 endpoints (health.internal.v4.redwood.net) and add a rollout to reduce concurrency from 200->50.
maya: +1. I'm going to open a config PR for the probe to force IPv4 and lower concurrency. Also ticket to add autoscale for NAT64 translator and increase ephemeral ports.
leila: FYI, costs: adding more NAT64 boxes will raise infra spend ~0.6% monthly; still cheaper than customer outages. Put cost estimate in the ticket.
ryan: Also add a fallback in the console: if >20% healthcheck failures in 5m and errors include ENOPROTOOPT, temporarily switch to IPv4 healthchecks automatically.
sam: I'll draft the automation. For now, roll the probe change at 12:40 UTC.
maya: Roll started. Will post results.
infra-bot: [DEPLOY] healthcheck-config update rolled to 50% at 12:42 UTC
maya: After the partial rollout healthcheck failures dropped to ~2% on affected nodes. :thumbsup:
leila: Nice. Follow-up items: increase ephemeral port range, add NAT64 autoscale, add console automated fallback, update docs on probe recommendations.
maya: Filed infra ticket INFRA-2892 with estimate and owner tags. Thanks everyone :rocket:
